ASSESSMENT-ALIGNED edition. Runs inside a DevRev `invoke_code` (Execute Code) node placed
BETWEEN the Ask AI node and the Router. It takes the (untrusted, non-deterministic) Ask AI
output and validates it into a safe, strongly-typed decision the Router branches on.

ALIGNMENT with the exercise (3 named paths only - no 4th Review path):
- The exercise's Router has EXACTLY three named paths: Bug / Feature / Enhancement.
- Therefore this embedded validator does NOT emit a "Review" route. Instead, on ANY invalid
  / malformed / unknown-label / empty-justification output it RAISES ValueError, which STOPS
  the workflow run (the run is marked failed in the Runs tab). There is no 4th route and no
  silent mutation on bad AI output.
- On a clean, in-enum result it returns `route` set to EXACTLY the accepted label
  (Bug/Feature/Enhancement) plus the trimmed justification. The Router matches `route` with a
  single-value `contains_any` list on each of the three named routes.

SECURITY: it NEVER uses eval/exec and NEVER interprets any field value as code. The untrusted
ticket title/body are handled in the Ask AI prompt (delimited, treated as DATA). This module
only type/shape/enum-checks the structured classifier output. In particular it does NOT run
JSONata `$eval` on the AI string - evaluating an untrusted model-produced expression would be
an injection vector.

DevRev Execute Code (Python) signature: `def run(inputs, keyrings)`.
"""

import json

ALLOWED_CLASSIFICATIONS = ("Bug", "Feature", "Enhancement")
DEFAULT_CLASSIFICATION_KEY = "classification"
DEFAULT_JUSTIFICATION_KEY = "justification"
MIN_JUSTIFICATION_LEN = 1
MAX_JUSTIFICATION_LEN = 1000

# Declared output field types - configure the Execute Code node outputs to match EXACTLY.
# NOTE: there is NO "Review"/"requires_review"/"approved" output in the aligned edition -
# an invalid classification raises ValueError and stops the run instead of routing to a 4th
# path.
OUTPUT_FIELDS = {
    "route": "text",           # the accepted label, always one of Bug/Feature/Enhancement
    "classification": "text",  # same accepted label (kept for comment templates)
    "justification": "text",   # trimmed justification
}


def _coerce_structured(ai_output):
    """Accept a dict (already-parsed) or a RAW JSON object string. Returns a dict or None.

    Strict: a bare JSON object only. Arrays/numbers/strings/bools/null, fenced blocks, and
    prose-wrapped blobs are rejected (return None). No value is ever eval'd or exec'd.
    """
    if isinstance(ai_output, dict):
        return ai_output
    if isinstance(ai_output, str):
        text = ai_output.strip()
        if not text or text.startswith("```") or not text.startswith("{"):
            return None
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(text)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return None
        return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
    return None


def validate_classification_strict(
    ai_output,
    classification_key=DEFAULT_CLASSIFICATION_KEY,
    justification_key=DEFAULT_JUSTIFICATION_KEY,
):
    """Pure, testable core. Returns {route, classification, justification} for a clean,
    in-enum result. RAISES ValueError (stops the workflow run) on ANY invalid input - there
    is no Review route in the aligned 3-path design. Never mutates its input.
    """
    data = _coerce_structured(ai_output)
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError("Classifier output was missing or not valid structured JSON/object.")

    label = data.get(classification_key)
    if not isinstance(label, str):
        raise ValueError("Classification field was missing or not a string.")
    if label not in ALLOWED_CLASSIFICATIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            "Classification was not one of the allowed labels (Bug/Feature/Enhancement)."
        )

    justification = data.get(justification_key)
    if not isinstance(justification, str):
        raise ValueError("Justification was missing or not a string.")
    justification = justification.strip()
    if len(justification) < MIN_JUSTIFICATION_LEN:
        raise ValueError("Justification was empty.")
    if len(justification) > MAX_JUSTIFICATION_LEN:
        raise ValueError(
            "Justification exceeded the maximum allowed length (%d chars)." % MAX_JUSTIFICATION_LEN
        )

    return {
        "route": label,            # Router matches this against Bug/Feature/Enhancement
        "classification": label,
        "justification": justification,
    }


def run(inputs, keyrings):
    """DevRev Execute Code entrypoint.

    Input: ai_output - the Ask AI node's structured output (dict) OR its raw JSON string.
    Output (configure node outputs to match): route (text), classification (text),
    justification (text). Invalid AI output RAISES ValueError and the run fails - there is no
    4th Review path.
    """
    inputs = inputs or {}
    return validate_classification_strict(inputs.get("ai_output"))

Runs inside a DevRev `invoke_code` (Execute Code) node on the Bug path. Validates the ticket
title against an ASSUMED format and returns a structured result the workflow branches on and
quotes in a comment. The exercise does NOT define a Bug title format, so `^\[BUG\] .{5,120}$`
is a stated assumption - adjust in the sandbox if the grader expects otherwise. No AI
determinism is assumed; malformed/empty input is handled safely (never raises).

DevRev Execute Code (Python) signature: `def run(inputs, keyrings)`.
"""

import re

BUG_TITLE_PATTERN = r"^\[BUG\] .{5,120}$"
_BUG_TITLE_RE = re.compile(BUG_TITLE_PATTERN)


def validate_bug_title(title):
    if not isinstance(title, str):
        return {"is_valid": False, "reason": "Title was missing or not a string.",
                "normalized_title": "", "pattern": BUG_TITLE_PATTERN}
    normalized = title.strip()
    if not normalized:
        return {"is_valid": False, "reason": "Title was empty after trimming whitespace.",
                "normalized_title": "", "pattern": BUG_TITLE_PATTERN}
    is_valid = _BUG_TITLE_RE.match(normalized) is not None
    reason = ("Title matches the assumed Bug format." if is_valid
              else "Title does not match the assumed Bug format '[BUG] <5-120 chars>'.")
    return {"is_valid": is_valid, "reason": reason, "normalized_title": normalized,
            "pattern": BUG_TITLE_PATTERN}


def run(inputs, keyrings):
    inputs = inputs or {}
    return validate_bug_title(inputs.get("title"))
